contents.argument: Poisson bivector and bracket conventions; local coordinate formulation. The local definition also fixes the tensor transition law and permits degenerate bivectors.
Coordinate Jacobi and Schouten self-bracket conventions; the source leaves part of the verification as an exercise, so the complete chart-gluing and coordinate proof is local.
Formal coefficient, bidifferential, unit, and first-order Poisson normalization conventions.
Formal differential gauge maps and the convention for their action on star products.
Hochschild differential, shifted degree, signed insertions, and bracket convention.
Shifted Hochschild bracket and differential identities. The local proof supplies the complete insertion pre-Lie and Jacobi calculations and the normalized multidifferential closure argument.

contents.locator: §4.2.5, Hochschild DGLA and Maurer–Cartan discussion (PDF pp. 96–98)
contents.argument: Hochschild obstruction framework. The exact finite-order cocycle and extension criterion are fully derived locally from associativity and the DGLA identities.
First-order gauge transformation. The local proof expands T and T inverse and checks the Hochschild coboundary sign against the library's delta convention.

Moyal exponential product for a constant Poisson tensor. The local proof gives coefficientwise finiteness, associativity on three tensor factors, degeneracy cases, and the canonical symplectic sign calculation.

contents.argument: Formal product coefficient and associativity conventions; local definition states the finite coefficient convolution and unit explicitly.

Associativity imposes the first-order commutator Lie and biderivation identities. The local proof derives both directly from the exact associative commutator identities.
Gerstenhaber insertion and shifted bracket conventions; the local proof supplies the pre-Lie identity, Jacobi, and differential derivation in full.
Order-n Hochschild obstruction and extension equation; the local proof additionally establishes normalized multidifferential closure and states only a one-order criterion.
